larval growth rate is a major determinant of spat growth rate in Crassostreas gigas, and the size grading of larvae in bivale hatcheries is a good way to increase spat growth rate and production.
the growth rate of oyster spat depends on larval size at metamorphosis.
the size of larvae at the time of metamorphosis has a significant effect on growth of the juveniles.

the relationship between larval growth and spat growth.
the genetic and environmental factors influencing the growth and production of Crassostrea gias.
the relationship between the growth of larvae and spat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the size grading of larvae in bivlave hatcheries is justified and the early growth is of great importance on growth in later stage in C. gigas.
the growth rate of oysters during the larval phase is a major determinant of the growth of oysters during their juvenile and adult phases.
the growth rate of oysters is a function of both larval size and the developmental age at settlement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the larval growth rate is a good predictor for spat growth rate and for the total weight of spat at the end of intensive culture.
the growth in the first few days after settlement is the most important determinant for growth during the rest of the life of the oyster.
the size of the larvae at the time of metamorphosis is an important factor in determining growth in the juvenile and adult stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the size of larvae has a direct impact on the size of juveniles and that size grading of larvae can improve spat yield.
it shows that the growth of larvae and spat is highly correlated, which means that the growth of spat is highly correlated with the growth of the larvae from which they are derived.
the growth of the oyster larvae is an important determinant of the growth of juvenile oysters.
